newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FOREIGN FIRMS BID FOR BULGARIAN COPPER PRODUCER.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN FIRMS BID FOR BULGARIAN COPPER PRODUCER.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency started negotiations on Wednesday with foreign firms interested in buying 56 percent of the MDK copper smelter, agency officials said.

MDK executive director Alexander Alexandrov said the bidders included Belgium's Union Miniere SA and Swiss firm Glencore International. Korea's Daewoo handed in its offer after the deadline expired on April 24.
"Glencor has been our partner in selling our production and raw material supplies," he told Reuters.
He said another 30 percent of the plant had been offered for mass voucher privatisation.

"MDK's integration with a powerful company will guarantee its future with direct access on the international metal market and investments for expansion and environmental improvements at the plant," he said.
Alexandrov said renovation of the plant would help reduce pollution.
The World Bank said last December it was willing to help finance capacity expansion, upgrading and solving environmental problems of MDK once the company is privatised.
The bank said the smelter's current electrolytic refinery, producing refined copper, needed to be replaced by a much larger refinery.
"In June we plan to start reconstruction of the sulphur acid installations, which would cost us some $300,000," Alexandrov said.

The smelter, which imports some 30 percent of its raw materials, made a profit of more than 2.4 billion levs last year and some $3 million in 1995, Alexandrov said. He was unable to comment on its debts.
Turnover was $111.4 million in 1994 and $168 million in 1995, privatisation agency figures show.
The plant's annual copper production capacity is up to 50,000 tonnes. Its equipment dates back to 1958.
